chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who recites the Talbiyyah for Hajj or Umrah, but does not intend the Hajj. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid, and it is not befitting for him to do so.'

key_terms.لَبَّى: To recite the Talbiyyah (the ritual declaration of readiness to meet God) during Hajj or Umrah.
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ: It is not valid / It counts for nothing.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting the Talbiyyah for Hajj without intending to perform Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that merely reciting the Talbiyyah without the specific internal intention (niyyah) for Hajj is insufficient and not befitting, highlighting the Shia emphasis on niyyah as the foundational pillar that validates ritual acts. This ruling underscores the principle that outward recitation alone does not constitute worship without the accompanying spiritual resolve, a key distinction in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the conditions of validity.
